newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto denounces Leghari for husband's detention.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto denounces Leghari for husband's detention.

text.p: Ousted Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto denounced President Farooq Leghari on Wednesday for "brutal" treatment of her detained husband and said she prayed that God would punish him.
"I write to protest against the inhuman, barbaric and brutal treatment being meted out to my husband, Asif Ali Zardari, Minister of Investment," Bhutto wrote to the president.
Her letter was received by fax from the secretariat of her Pakistan People's Party (PPP).
Leghari's spokesman could not be reached for comment.

"You made him work night and day to get you elected as president," Bhutto wrote. "Now while you sit in the luxurious surroundings of the presidency where the blood of our martyrs and the suffering of our people put you, you have had Asif Ali Zardari put in solitary confinement and treated worse than a common criminal."
Zardari was detained in Lahore after Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Held under a catch-all maintenance of public order law, he was transferred to a resthouse near Islamabad and later to the southern city of Karachi.
"Yesterday you had him put in a cage to meet his lawyer," Bhutto wrote. "You are denying him medical treatment for his ulcers.

"Take your sadistic pleasure. Be ungrateful. Treat us shamelessly. But remember there is a God watching all this. It is my prayer to the Almighty Allah that he may punish you for what you are doing to our nation and to its sons and daughters.

"If this is the way the husband of the prime minister and a cabinet minister can be kept, then that means there is no law. But do not forget there is divine law and its retribution no one can prevent," Bhutto wrote.

The caretaker government of Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has said it will bring undisclosed charges against Bhutto and Zardari, who was at the centre of corruption allegations swirling round the former government. Both deny any wrongdoing.
Leghari, once a close political associate of Bhutto, was her nominee for president after the PPP and its allies won the October 1993 election.
After removing Bhutto, he said fresh elections to the National Assembly (lower house) would be held on February 3.
